title: What happens to 23 × 27 when both numbers change by 1?
description: Twenty three times twenty seven is six hundred twenty one. Treating each bracket as one number and distributing twice shows the change when both numbers go up by one, and when one goes up and one comes down. Keeko doubts that a rise and a fall cancel.
teaching_notes: One idea: expand the two brackets with the distributive property, and the change is everything beyond the old product. Watch for students who think one more and one less always cancel.

source: 23 × 27 = 621. Find the change in the product when both numb
video_script.why: The child knows how one number's growth changes a total, and now meets both numbers changing at once.
video_script.substitution: Treat a plus one as a single number, distribute twice, and read the change from the expanded form.
video_script.anchor: the book's twenty three rows and twenty seven columns of dots, with a bracket for each side
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says one number goes up and one comes down by the same step, so the total stays the same. The new total is six hundred twenty four against six hundred twenty one, so it changes by three.
video_script.payoff_line: Expanding the brackets shows how the total changes

final_answer.value: Both up by 1: the product increases by 51; one up and one down: it increases by 3
final_answer.spoken: when both go up by one the total grows by fifty one, and when one goes up and one comes down it grows by three

never_show: a total that stays the same, marked as right
maths_rules: (a + 1)(b + 1) = (a + 1)b + (a + 1) × 1 = ab + b + a + 1; the increase is a + b + 1
(a + 1)(b − 1) = (a + 1)b − (a + 1) × 1 = ab + b − a − 1; the change is b − a − 1
video_script.design: One idea: expand the brackets and read the change beyond the old product. Assumes the distributive property. Wrong idea: a rise and a fall cancel. The old block of dots and the expanded lines stay in view.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='grid'/>Twenty three times twenty seven is six hundred twenty one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>By how much does this change if both numbers grow by one? What if twenty three grows by one while twenty seven shrinks by one?

beats.on_screen: the two question tags stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the bracket (a + 1) is boxed as one number beside the bracket (b + 1); the words expand = remove the brackets appear

marks.one: the bracket (a + 1) is boxed and treated as one number
marks.dist: an arrow shows it multiplying each part of (b + 1)
marks.exp: the word expand appears with its meaning

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>A bracket can be treated as one single number.
<bookmark mark='dist'/>The distributive property can then multiply it with each part of the other bracket.
<bookmark mark='exp'/>To expand means to write the same value without the brackets.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, twenty three times twenty seven is six hundred twenty one.

beats.on_screen: To find: the change when both grow by 1; the change when 23 grows by 1 and 27 shrinks by 1

marks.find: the two changes are written as the two things to find

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the change when both numbers grow by one.
We also find the change when one grows and the other shrinks.

marks.second: ab + b + a + 1 is written under it
marks.extra: the three extra terms after ab light up

beats.colours: ab in one colour, the extra parts in another
narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, expand eigh plus one times b plus one.
Treat eigh plus one as one number, and distribute it over b plus one.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Distribute again, and the result is eigh b plus b plus eigh plus one.
<bookmark mark='extra'/>Beyond eigh b, the extra parts are b, eigh and one.

marks.values: a = 23 and b = 27 are put in, giving 23 + 27 + 1 = 51

narration: <bookmark mark='values'/>Step two, put eigh as twenty three and b as twenty seven.
The extra parts are twenty three, twenty seven and one.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check it. Twenty four times twenty eight is six hundred seventy two.
Six hundred seventy two take away six hundred twenty one is fifty one.

marks.second2: ab + b − a − 1 is written under it

beats.colours: ab in one colour, the extra parts in another
beats.removed: the lines of the first case
narration: <bookmark mark='first2'/>Step three, expand eigh plus one times b minus one the same way.
Distribute the first bracket, and keep the minus sign with the one.
<bookmark mark='second2'/>The result is eigh b plus b minus eigh minus one.
<bookmark mark='values2'/>Step four, the change is b minus eigh minus one.
That is twenty seven take away twenty three, take away one.
<bookmark mark='check2'/>Check it. Twenty four times twenty six is six hundred twenty four.
Six hundred twenty four take away six hundred twenty one is three.

beats.on_screen: Both up by 1: increase 51. One up, one down: increase 3.

marks.pay: the words expanding the brackets shows the change appear
marks.ans1: Both up by 1: increase 51 is boxed
marks.ans2: One up, one down: increase 3 is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Expanding the brackets shows how the total changes.
<bookmark mark='ans1'/>When both numbers go up by one, the total grows by fifty one.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>When one goes up and one comes down, it grows by three.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble shows 621 → 621 and is crossed out; 624 appears beside 621

marks.doubt: a bubble shows the old total unchanged

beats.colours: the wrong bubble in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the total stays the same, because one number goes up and one comes down.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the new total is six hundred twenty four, and the old total was six hundred twenty one.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The two are not equal, so a rise and a fall do not cancel.
